findings.title: Fabricator file contents were accidentally swapped
findings.body: The file spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now contains the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while all four category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category) were moved into the newly added spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The contents of the two files are swapped: the category fabricators belong in category_fabricator.rb and the embeddable_host fabricator belongs in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The suite still passes because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but any developer looking for the category fabricator in category_fabricator.rb will find the wrong definition, and future edits are likely to be applied to the wrong file.

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category / uncategorized_category_id rows are absent
findings.body: Line 11 does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. Site settings only exist as rows in the site_settings table when they have been changed from their YAML defaults, so on a fresh install (or any site that never set embed_category, or where the stored value is '' or doesn't match a category name) the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and the migration aborts with `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil`. The same crash exists on line 15 for the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup when that row doesn't exist. This makes `rake db:migrate` fail on exactly the databases this migration is supposed to upgrade. The code needs to handle empty result sets (e.g. `rows[0].try(:[], 'id')` with a fallback).

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted without normalization and may never match again
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting was matched leniently: `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` prefixes before comparing, so entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` worked. The new lookup (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`) requires an exact match against `URI(...).host`, and the model only strips the scheme/path in a `before_validation` callback — which never runs because this migration inserts the raw setting values with a bare SQL INSERT. Any existing entry that includes a scheme or path will be copied verbatim into the table and will silently stop matching referers after the upgrade, breaking comment embedding for those sites. The migration should normalize each value (strip scheme, path, and whitespace) before inserting.

findings.title: Migration interpolates host values into SQL without escaping
findings.body: The INSERT is built with string interpolation: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` where `h` comes from a free-form, admin-editable site setting that was never validated as a hostname. A value containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will produce a syntax error and abort the migration mid-way, leaving the site_settings rows already deleted on some paths. Use `quote(h)` / bound parameters or insert via the model instead of raw string interpolation.

findings.title: update and destroy crash with NoMethodError when the host record doesn't exist
findings.body: In `update`, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be nil, and `save_host(nil)` immediately calls `host.host = ...`, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. `destroy` has the same problem: `host.destroy` on nil raises. Both actions should return a 404 (e.g. `raise Discourse::NotFound`) when the record is missing, as other admin controllers do.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
findings.body: The before_validation block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `host` is nil — for example a POST to /admin/embeddable_hosts with a missing or blank `embeddable_host[host]` param — this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil` and the request 500s, rather than producing a validation error from the format validator. Guard with `if self.host` (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s.sub(...)`) so an empty value fails validation cleanly.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters
findings.body: The format regex ends with `\.[a-z]{2,5}`, which rejects legitimate hostnames with longer TLDs such as `example.technology`, `blog.international`, or `site.photography`. Admins embedding from such domains will get a validation error and be unable to add the host. The TLD portion should be more permissive (e.g. `[a-z]{2,}`).

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match in record_for_host
findings.body: The validation regex explicitly permits a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), so an admin can save `example.com:3000`. But `record_for_host` compares the stored value against `URI(host).host`, which never includes the port, so `where("lower(host) = ?", "example.com")` will not match the stored `example.com:3000`. Any host entry with a port is accepted by the UI but embedding from that host will always be rejected with 'invalid referer host'. Either strip/disallow ports at save time or include the port in the comparison.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicate, conflicting entries
findings.body: There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` and no unique index in the migration, so admins can create multiple rows with the same host pointing at different categories. `record_for_host` then returns whichever row `.first` happens to load, making the category that embedded topics land in nondeterministic. Add a model-level uniqueness validation (ideally case-insensitive, since lookup is on `lower(host)`) and a unique database index.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no functional test coverage
findings.body: Both new controller specs (admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert that the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. Nothing exercises create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts, host normalization on save, the default-to-uncategorized category behavior, missing-record handling, or staff-only access. Bugs like the nil-record NoMethodError in update/destroy would be caught by even a minimal request spec.

findings.title: edit() throws when the host's category no longer exists
findings.body: `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))` assumes `host.category` is always present. `EmbeddableHost` has no foreign-key or dependent handling, so if the referenced category is deleted, the serializer still emits the stale `category_id`, the client-side lookup in the store finds no category, and `host.category` is undefined — clicking the pencil button then throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'id' of undefined` and the row can no longer be edited. Use a safe access (`this.get('host.category.id')` via `Ember.get` chain or `host.get('category.id')` which is null-safe in Ember) and consider clearing category_id when a category is destroyed.
